AI Summary

Three papers are worth reading in full this cycle. Yamada et al. identify the histone reader SPIN1 as a TE-silencing pathway that recognizes chromatin state rather than DNA sequence or transcript structure: SPIN1 binds young LINE and ERV copies carrying both H3K4me3 and H3K9me3, requires SPINDOC as a cofactor, and associates with SETDB1 and G9a. That makes it a new targeting module for exactly the H3K9 methyltransferases whose inhibition drives TE derepression and viral mimicry in tumors, with an evolutionary-age filter built in. Courvan et al. show that METTL3 inhibition with STM2457 blunts the macrophage type I interferon response not at the effector genes but at the sensing machinery, reducing expression of the type I interferon receptor and STAT1, with human coronavirus OC43 replicating better as a consequence — a direct collision of the lab's m6A and IFNAR threads, and a baseline shift that any STM2457 experiment reading out interferon now has to account for. Aderounmu et al. resolve the second-strand nicking step of non-LTR retrotransposition, showing that a DNA-bound R2 protein recruits a second R2 copy once cDNA synthesis liberates the required domains, and that crippling this step shifts insertion junctions from small deletions to large duplications requiring extensive repair.

The m6A thread runs through the journal slate as well. Arco-Hierves et al. place METTL3 at the center of mitochondrial RNA surveillance in epithelium, with loss of that surveillance releasing mt-dsRNA as an endogenous type I interferon trigger in Sjogren's disease — the same writer the lab studies in TE-derived transcript control, here governing a different endogenous immunostimulatory RNA, and a reminder that interferon phenotypes following METTL3 perturbation have more than one possible source. Akcaoz-Alasar et al. add a second METTL3 complication from the opposite direction, wiring the enzyme into transcriptional elongation control at mitotic entry, which means METTL3 inhibitors can alter transcript architecture through a route entirely separate from methylation-dependent RNA decay. Read alongside Courvan et al., the practical message for TE exonization work is that STM2457 is a less clean tool than it appears: it moves interferon sensing, elongation, and m6A at once.

On the enhancer side, Guo et al. provide the cycle's best worked example of a large insertion becoming a long-range regulator: a 9.1-kb presence/absence variant at the maize HI1 locus acts as a distal enhancer for the response regulator BRR1 through a CONZ1/GCN5 chromatin loop, and was fixed by domestication selection — the LTR10/MER41 co-option story with the looping mechanism actually solved. Zhang et al. make the reference-representation argument in crop terms, using a 16-accession graph pangenome and 123,131 structural variants to recover wild alleles a linear reference cannot see. Jay et al. trace single alleles in CD4+ T cells and find that cytokine cues reposition the Ets1 super-enhancer rather than simply switching it on — the kind of allele-resolved geometry that population-average Hi-C would blur at a polymorphic immune locus. Ou et al. show one Zeb2 enhancer directing several independent lineage decisions through distinct motif classes, which they call site-specific pleiotropy and which is a good frame for why the motif complement a co-opted TE brings is the whole story. Iliadou et al. supply the accompanying Perspective on why long-range enhancer action is the norm rather than the exception.

Interferon gain control recurs across the immune slate. Deng et al. add SET7 monomethylation of IRF3 at lysine 98 as a brake on phosphorylation, dimerization and nuclear entry; Lenhard et al. show CD73 sets neutrophil responsiveness to type I interferon without changing IFNAR levels, the mirror image of a decoy receptor isoform acting from the receptor side; and Poirier et al. show that dual PTPN1/PTPN2 loss amplifies STAT1/3/5 signaling and MHC-I but raises PD-L1 in step — a caveat that applies directly to TE-derepression strategies, since turning up tumor interferon output also turns up the brake. Two papers deliver endogenous-DNA interferon triggers by new routes: Li et al. via SADS-CoV-induced chromatin leakage and DAD1-dependent STING trafficking, and Romero et al. via nuclear DNA expelled into the cytoplasm on viral fusion. Method-wise, Jung et al. close a real bottleneck with virus-like-particle delivery of CRISPR knockout, base editing and epigenetic silencing plus Perturb-seq in primary human macrophages and dendritic cells, and Zheng and Sedlazeck add the prevalence layer long-read isoform discovery has lacked, scoring user-submitted transcript models against 1,035 human and 414 mouse long-read samples. One coverage caveat on this issue: the bioRxiv scan was truncated by repeated API timeouts at 1,020 of 3,626 available records, so the preprint slate below is drawn from roughly 28% of the window's preprints and should not be read as a complete survey. The journal side is complete, with 18 of 20 feeds returning over RSS and Genome Research and Molecular Biology and Evolution covered by the PubMed fallback.
